site.name: Bueno Mill
overview: Bueno Mill is the historic ore-processing complex also documented as the Wano Mill and Williamson Mill near Jamestown. Federal records state that the site first processed gold ore and later converted to fluorspar processing.

The mill's history also survives through 1944 interior photographs and through federal cleanup records for its tailings. EPA investigations identified substantial metal-bearing tailings, leading to stabilization work in the 2000s and repairs after the 2013 Boulder County flood.

timeline.text: Historic photographs documented the interior of the Wano Mill—also identified as Bueno Mill or Williamson Mill—and its ore-processing operations.
EPA began a removal action after watershed studies identified metal-bearing mill tailings affecting James Creek and Little James Creek; the original stabilization work was completed in 2006.

Severe flooding damaged portions of the streamside tailings remedy. EPA carried out emergency stabilization and erosion-control repairs to reduce the risk of tailings reaching downstream water supplies.

moreHistory: EPA describes the Bueno and Streamside tailings deposits as containing an estimated 50,000 cubic yards of material.
The site is in the Jamestown Mining District between James Creek and Little James Creek, with the Bueno tailings on the intervening ridge.
Remnant uses EPA's listed Bueno Mill and Mine site coordinate as a site-level identification point. It does not identify a particular surviving mill structure, mine opening, or public access route.
